title: Dedicated Throughput Tiers — Tier Matrix v1
content:
TAB: Overview (readme)
Owner: Lauren Bishop
Last updated: 2025-02-05

Purpose
- Working v1 matrix to align Product + SRE + Infra + Sales on Dedicated tier definitions.
- This is NOT customer-facing language; final wording will live in Confluence + contracts.

Primary metric (v1 assumption)
- Throughput guarantee expressed as: sustained successful OUTPUT tokens/sec per deployment (aggregate across all replicas in the Dedicated pool), measured over a rolling window.
- Window: 5-minute rolling average (subject to SRE review) for reporting; alerting may use shorter windows.
- "Successful" excludes customer-caused 4xx, cancellations, and requests rejected due to explicit admission control (i.e., throttling is not an SLO breach).

Workload assumptions (for interpreting targets below)
- Model family: Redwood verified open-weight chat models (7B–70B). Baselines below are calibrated on a representative 13B/34B class model unless otherwise noted.
- Prompt length distribution: p50 512 tok, p95 2,048 tok.
- Output length distribution: p50 256 tok, p95 1,024 tok.
- Streaming: on (server-sent events).
- Concurrency assumption: steady-state concurrency at or below tier "Included concurrency".

Notes
- Exact numbers likely move after benchmark suite normalization + safety factor agreement.
- Regional availability constrained by GPU supply; Premium is intentionally limited.


TAB: Tier Matrix v1

Legend
- Sustained throughput target = internal target used to set SLO objective thresholds.
- Guaranteed minimum (contractable) = target after safety factor / exclusions; requires Legal + Finance sign-off.
- Included concurrency = concurrency level the guarantee assumes (not a hard limit; admission control may enforce max concurrency per tier).
- Burst = temporary higher throughput above sustained guarantee, subject to guardrails.

| Tier | Intended customer | Guaranteed minimum (contractable) OUTPUT tok/s | Sustained throughput target (internal) OUTPUT tok/s | Included concurrency (steady-state) | Tail latency guardrail (decode) | Burst policy (v1) | Overload behavior | Failover / routing | Reporting / exports | Support & escalation |
|------|-------------------|-----------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|-------------------------------|------------------|------------------|-------------------|--------------------|---------------------|
| Standard | predictable baseline capacity, cost-sensitive | 8,000 tok/s per deployment pool | 10,000 tok/s | 32 concurrent streams | p95 time-to-first-token <= 1.5s; p95 inter-token <= 60ms (under assumptions) | Up to +50% above guarantee for 10 min / hr if headroom exists | Throttle first (429 + Retry-After). Queue depth capped. No shedding unless platform incident. | Optional multi-zone within region; no cross-region failover by default | Daily CSV export + Console dashboard (7d retention) | P1 response 4h (business hours) |
| Performance | latency-sensitive + higher concurrency | 20,000 tok/s | 25,000 tok/s | 64 concurrent streams | p95 TTFT <= 1.2s; p95 inter-token <= 45ms | Up to 2x guarantee for 15 min / hr (subject to fleet headroom + admission control limits) | Throttle at soft limit; enter "overload mode" to protect tail latency (reduce max concurrency, tighten batching) | Multi-zone in-region included; optional warm standby in second region (paid add-on) | Hourly export + dashboard (14d retention); per-route + per-model breakdown | P1 response 2h (24/5) |
| Premium | strict SLOs, regulated workflows, exec visibility | 40,000 tok/s | 50,000 tok/s | 128 concurrent streams | p95 TTFT <= 1.0s; p95 inter-token <= 35ms | Up to 2.5x guarantee for 20 min / hr (requires pre-provisioned burst buffer) | Admission control engaged early; may shed lowest-priority traffic by policy (customer-configured) | In-region + cross-region failover option; priority routing in capacity events | Near-real-time export (5-min), dashboard (30d retention), customer-visible SLO report | P1 response 1h (24/7), named escalation |

Footnotes / clarifications (v1)
1) The tok/s guarantee is for output tokens (decode) only. Prefill cost variance is handled via assumptions + exclusions; we may add a separate "prefill budget" later.
2) If customer workload exceeds documented context/length distribution materially, we reserve the right to re-baseline or move to a higher tier/shape.
3) If we throttle due to admission control to preserve SLOs, that is considered expected behavior, not an SLO miss.


TAB: Supported shapes & regional availability (v1)

Shape naming (internal shorthand)
- "S" = single node; "M" = multi-node (NVLink/IB where applicable)
- All shapes are Dedicated GPU pools with tenant isolation.
- MIG: only allowed on select Standard shapes; not allowed for Performance/Premium (v1).

| Shape ID | GPUs | GPU type | CPU/RAM | Network | Storage | MIG allowed | Notes | Eligible tiers | Regions (initial) |
|----------|------|----------|---------|---------|---------|------------|-------|---------------|------------------|
| S-L4-1 | 1x | NVIDIA L4 24GB | 16 vCPU / 128GB | 25GbE | 1TB NVMe | Yes | best-effort for smaller models; limited headroom | Standard | us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 |
| S-L4-4 | 4x | NVIDIA L4 24GB | 64 vCPU / 512GB | 50GbE | 2TB NVMe | No | preferred Standard default | Standard | us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 |
| S-L40S-2 | 2x | NVIDIA L40S 48GB | 64 vCPU / 512GB | 50GbE | 2TB NVMe | No | more stable decode latency vs L4 | Standard, Performance (limited) | us-east-1, eu-central-1 (limited) |
| S-A100-1 | 1x | NVIDIA A100 80GB | 64 vCPU / 512GB | 50GbE | 2TB NVMe | No | baseline for Performance small/medium models | Performance | us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 |
| S-A100-8 | 8x | NVIDIA A100 80GB | 128 vCPU / 1TB | 100GbE | 4TB NVMe | No | NVLink; strong for 34B–70B | Performance, Premium (case-by-case) | us-east-1, us-west-2 (constrained), eu-west-1 (constrained) |
| S-H100-8 | 8x | NVIDIA H100 80GB | 128 vCPU / 1TB | 200GbE | 4TB NVMe | No | default Premium target shape | Premium | us-east-1 (priority), us-west-2 (limited) |
| M-H100-16 | 16x | NVIDIA H100 80GB | 256 vCPU / 2TB | IB/NVSwitch | 8TB NVMe | No | for very high throughput + redundancy | Premium (exceptions only) | us-east-1 (special order) |

Region availability notes (v1)
- Premium is gated by supply. Vanessa/Irene to publish weekly capacity notes until general availability.
- EMEA: expect limited A100/H100 initially; default to L4/L40S for Standard in eu-west-1.


TAB: Feature toggles by tier (v1)

| Capability | Standard | Performance | Premium | Notes |
|------------|----------|-------------|---------|------|
| Admission control policies (max concurrency, queue depth caps) | On | On | On | Enforcement mechanism for preventing SLO risk |
| Burst | Limited | Yes | Yes+ | Requires headroom; may be disabled during incidents |
| Customer-configurable priority classes | No | Limited (2 classes) | Yes (multi-class) | Needed for overload mode shedding policy |
| Multi-zone redundancy | Optional | Included | Included | Within same region |
| Cross-region failover | No | Add-on | Optional/Included depending on contract | Requires warm standby + routing policy |
| Customer-visible throughput dashboard | Basic | Full | Full + SLO report | Console surface area minimal for v1 |
| Exportable metrics | Daily | Hourly | 5-min | CSV initially; API later |
| Audit log retention | 7d | 30d | 90d | Contract-dependent |
| Dedicated oncall coverage | 24/5 | 24/5 | 24/7 | Premium has named escalation |


TAB: Pricing inputs (placeholders for Finance)

Do NOT share outside Redwood.

| Tier | Target gross margin | Utilization assumption (avg) | Notes / risk |
|------|---------------------|-----------------------------|-------------|
| Standard | 55–60% | 55% | most sensitive to burst policy (headroom) |
| Performance | 60–65% | 65% | assume stronger predictability / reserved commits |
| Premium | 65%+ | 70% | supply-constrained; price reflects priority allocation |

Open items for Rishi/Laura
- Define how to price burst buffer capacity (separate line item vs embedded).
- Discount guardrails by tier + min term.


TAB: Open questions / TODO (as of 2025-02-05)
- Confirm primary metric phrasing: output tok/s vs total tok/s (prefill+decode). (Owner: Lauren + Omar)
- Decide final rolling window for SLO evaluation (5m vs 10m) and alert windows. (Owner: Aisha + Rafael)
- Confirm whether Standard should allow MIG at all (cardinality + noisy neighbor even in dedicated pools). (Owner: Irene + Sofia Ivanova)
- Decide if "Guaranteed minimum" should be a single number or a table by model class (e.g., <=13B, 34B, 70B). (Owner: Lauren)
- Clarify contract language around throttling vs breach; ensure Support can explain clearly. (Owner: Michael Grant + Sofia Mendes)
- Align tier names with GTM ("Performance" vs "Plus"). (Owner: Jordan Blake)

Recent changes log
- 2025-01-28: added explicit "Included concurrency" column; earlier drafts assumed 32 for all.
- 2025-02-03: added Premium cross-region failover option + reporting cadence row.
- 2025-02-05: updated shape list to include L40S-2 as Standard/Performance bridge based on fleet notes.
